clue.text: East German wealth is strictly for the birds

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east
riches means wealth

explanation.surface: An East German's fortune is said to be utterly worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strictly for the birds' reads as the idiom for something worthless, but 'the birds' is the definition and 'is strictly for' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostriches are large flightless African birds.

clue.text: Beginning where the film folk work

definitions.meaning: actors and crew work on the set, read as two words

explanation.surface: The start of the day in a film studio.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is a start; read as two words it is the location of filming.

clue.text: Does capital if boring work

parts.note: capital means head, so the boring work is drilling into a skull

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone does dull jobs excellently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as 'excellent' and 'boring' as 'dull', but capital is the head and boring is drilling: the surgeon bores the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: To trepan is to cut a hole in the skull with a surgical saw.

clue.text: Aid for writers when the marker is upright

definitions.text: Aid for writers when the marker is upright

parts.words: Aid for writers when the marker is upright
parts.note: the marker is ink, and upright means it stands

explanation.surface: A writing aid used when the pen is held vertically.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a sentence, the answer says ink stands; as one word it is a desk holder for ink bottles and pens.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkstands hold ink and pens on a writing desk.

clue.text: Pledge note after fixer gets the cat

indicators.note: after says the note comes behind the other pieces

parts.note: hypo is sodium thiosulphate, the photographic fixer
taken as written
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A promissory note given after a repairman catches the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixer' suggests a mender, but in photography hypo fixes the image.
explanation.definitionFit: To hypothecate is to pledge property as security for a debt.

clue.text: Medical bag

parts.note: not a doctor's case but a pouch in the body

explanation.surface: A doctor's carrying case.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a doctor's bag; the answer is a pouch-like structure in anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy a sac is a pouch or cavity in the body.

clue.text: He gains nothing when he is less fast

definitions.meaning: someone who ends up with nothing from a contest or deal
the runner who is slower than the winner in a race

explanation.surface: A man who wins nothing because he is not quick enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser comes away empty-handed, and in a race the beaten runner is the slower one.

clue.text: Keep at it to avoid being locked up

definitions.text: Keep at it to avoid being locked up

parts.words: Keep at it to avoid being locked up
parts.note: keep the phrase at ... and you remain free

explanation.surface: Encouragement to persevere so as to stay out of prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep at it' sounds like 'persevere', but it means put the word after 'at': at large means free.
explanation.definitionFit: Large follows at in the phrase meaning free and not captured.

clue.text: Saint converted about a thousand — what endurance!

indicators.note: about says the rearranged saint goes around the other pieces
converted says the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A saint who converted around a thousand people showed great endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' rearranges SAINT into STINA, and 'about' puts it around A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the staying power to endure prolonged effort.

clue.text: The rascals smuggle precious stones

parts.note: to run guns or rum is to smuggle them
agates are semi-precious stones

explanation.surface: Villains caught smuggling gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Runagates is an old word for vagabonds, renegades and scoundrels.

clue.text: Don't mumble about the mountain when in drink

indicators.note: in says the mountain word is placed inside the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a peak is a mountain

explanation.surface: A climber told to stop mumbling while drinking near the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk louder and more clearly is the opposite of mumbling, an imperative instruction.

clue.text: Hanging is abrupt with the Scot's Own

parts.note: curt means abrupt or brusque
ain is Scots dialect for own

explanation.surface: An execution described as sudden, carried out by a Scottish regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests execution, but it is a noun: a drape. AIN is the Scots word for 'own'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape hung at a window or stage front is a hanging.

clue.text: Characteristic of Electra, it appears

indicators.note: appears says the answer shows itself within the words Electra, it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that something seems typical of Electra, the tragic heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'appears' as the definition, but 'Characteristic' is the definition: TRAIT is a noun, and 'appears' signals that it shows inside 'ElecTRA, IT'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing feature or quality of a person.

clue.text: Ramming without roundabout interference

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the ramming word goes around the other piece

parts.note: tamping is ramming down, as with earth or a charge
about is RE, and round turns it back to front, so the whole word gives the reversed pair

explanation.surface: A ship ramming another without going round it causes interference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking; 'roundabout' looks like a traffic island but is read as RE (about) turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampering is meddling or improper interference with something.

clue.text: In full, let me arrange it, sweet

indicators.note: arrange tells the solver to put these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asking to arrange a piece in full because it is sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellifluent means honey-flowing, sweetly smooth in sound.

clue.text: Firm's salad-maker

definitions.meaning: Co. is the abbreviation for company, so a firm's is Co.'s
a long-leaved lettuce used in salads

explanation.surface: A company that makes salads.
explanation.definitionFit: Co. abbreviates company, possessive Co.'s; the cos lettuce is a salad staple.

clue.text: Man is unlikely to produce such bulrushes

definitions.text: Man is unlikely to produce such
definitions.meaning: the Isle of Man breeds the Manx cat, which has no tail

explanation.surface: A remark that humans rarely grow reeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, home of the tailless Manx cat, not mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: The furry tails of cats and the reedmace's spikes share the plant's common name.

clue.text: Skill needed to bring Egypt's gift to the Embankment ?

definitions.text: Skill needed to bring Egypt's gift to the Embankment ?

parts.words: Skill needed to bring Egypt's gift to the Embankment ?
parts.note: Cleopatra's Needle, given by Egypt, stands on London's Victoria Embankment; the vessel that brought it would be the obelisk's craft

explanation.surface: Asks what ability was required to transport an Egyptian present to the Thames riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra's Needle is an Egyptian obelisk on the Victoria Embankment by the Thames in London; it was shipped over in a purpose-built vessel. The phrase also means sewing skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing and embroidery are crafts done with a needle.

clue.text: Maybe I can store the dressmaker's products

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be in another order

explanation.surface: A dressmaker musing that she might keep her goods in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A couturier's designs are called creations.

clue.text: My Bonnie's situation

parts.note: the song says my Bonnie lies over the ocean, so her position is beyond the sea

explanation.surface: Describes where the singer's sweetheart is.
explanation.walkthrough: The folk song 'My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean' places her across the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmarine means situated beyond or across the sea.

clue.text: Flower books ?

definitions.meaning: plants that flower and die within one year

explanation.surface: Books about flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuals are one-season plants and also yearly publications such as children's yearbooks.

clue.text: It's madly poetic

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective naming a poetic form; the answer is that poetic contraction itself

indicators.note: madly says the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something is wildly lyrical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' rearranges ITS; the result is the old poetic contraction of 'it is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction of it is with the apostrophe first belongs to verse and archaic diction.

clue.text: Apprentice railwayman ?

definitions.meaning: read as train plus the -ee ending, a person of the train

explanation.surface: A trainee working on the railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee learns a job; split, the word suggests someone tied to trains.

clue.text: You need a decimal eye to measure the ringer

definitions.text: You need a decimal eye to measure the ringer

parts.words: You need a decimal eye to measure the ringer
parts.note: the reading plays on ten (decimal) and the bel, the unit of loudness, with a ringer being a church bell

explanation.surface: Advises using a precise metric gaze to size up a bell-ringer.
explanation.walkthrough: A ringer here is a bell in a church peal; the clue toys with TEN and the bel, the acoustic unit.
explanation.definitionFit: In a ring of church bells the largest, lowest-pitched one has the voice name tenor.

clue.text: Academician is noted for breed

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
taken as written
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A Royal Academy artist known for his pedigree.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise animals or crops is to breed them.

clue.text: She ran in races with good companions

indicators.note: in says the word ran is placed inside the races abbreviation

parts.note: TT stands for the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman who competed in races with friendly teammates.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Elizabeth Trant runs the touring concert party in J. B. Priestley's novel 'The Good Companions', so 'with good companions' points to her.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Trant is a heroine of Priestley's 1929 novel, so she is a woman.

clue.text: Mind about the right drift

indicators.note: about says the word for mind goes around the other letter

parts.note: to tend is to mind or look after
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A warning to watch for the political shift to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a general direction or tendency, as in the drift of opinion.

clue.text: Story of " The Mousetrap was " written in very choice "

definitions.text: Story of " The Mousetrap was " written in very choice

parts.words: Story of " The Mousetrap was " written in very choice
parts.note: in Hamlet, the prince says of the play-within-the-play that the story is extant and written in a choice tongue

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quotation about the play staged in Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Mousetrap' is Hamlet's play within the play (Act III, scene 2), and Hamlet says its story is 'written in very choice Italian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Hamlet completes the line with the language of Italy.

clue.text: Find fault with a horse

explanation.surface: Criticising a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag is to carp at someone; a nag is also a broken-down horse.

clue.text: Proclaim or point to substantive religion

parts.note: E is east, a compass point
a substantive is the grammarian's word for a noun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Asked to proclaim a belief or point to a real, solid faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substantive' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it is a noun in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to state or declare formally.

clue.text: Army seamstress

parts.note: the First World War song 'Sister ... Sewing Shirts for Soldiers' names a woman sewing for the army

explanation.surface: A woman who sews uniforms for the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1914 music-hall song 'Sister Susie's Sewing Shirts for Soldiers' supplies the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's heroine sews shirts for soldiers, making her the troops' needlewoman.

clue.text: Restricts the principal town in Durham

parts.note: to gate a student is to confine them to college, so gates means restricts
a head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: The main town of County Durham imposing restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: To gate is the British school and university punishment of confining a pupil to the grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateshead is a town on the south bank of the Tyne, historically in County Durham.
